description: Senator Tina Smith (D) Minnesota discusses the possible supplemental funding request related to the Middle East conflict and expresses strong resistance to approving additional funding. She also talks about needing ICE to change their tactics in order to reopen DHS and shares the latest on the Senate housing bill. Senator Smith speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Deeply Concerned About Strategy, Cost of War: Sen. Smith

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Catherine Lucey
description: President Donald Trump’s administration started the first of several sweeping trade investigations that set the stage for new tariffs, the centerpiece of a push to replace levies struck down by the US Supreme Court.
title: US Launches Trade Probe Into China, EU in Trump’s Tariffs Revival

author: Mirette Magdy
description: Egyptian assets have been among the Middle East’s worst hit by the Iran war, a major stress test for grueling International Monetary Fund-backed reforms meant to protect against future crises.
title: Ripples From Iran War Put Egypt’s Resilience Under Spotlight

author: Ari Natter
description: The Trump administration plans to release 172 million barrels from the US emergency oil reserve as part of the coordinated effort by nations around the world to ease surging crude and fuel prices amid the Iran war.
title: US to Release 172 Million Barrels of Oil for IEA Relief Plan

author: Caitlin Reilly
description: A bipartisan congressional delegation will head to China in May, following President Donald Trump’s visit to the country.
title: Trump Ally to Lead High-Level Senate Delegation to China in May

author: Nicolle Yapur, Andreina Itriago
description: The government of Venezuela’s acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, was recognized by the US government in ongoing litigation related to the South American nation — another step by Washington toward legitimizing her authority.
title: Rodríguez Recognized as ‘Sole’ Venezuela Leader by US in Court

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump repeatedly lashed out at Representative Thomas Massie, one of his party’s most prominent critics of the Iran war, during a visit to the lawmaker’s Kentucky district, calling him “disloyal” and urging voters to back a primary challenger.
title: Trump Assails War Critic Massie as ‘Disloyal’ in Kentucky Visit

description: Brian Chappatta and Olivia Fishlow unpack the recent tumult in the world of private credit on the Big Take Podcast. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Private Credit’s Redemption Pressure Roller Coaster

description: Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin says the price tag for a prolonged conflict with Iran is likely “very, very high” and signals she won’t support supplemental funding for the Pentagon without a clearer breakdown of how existing defense dollars are being spent. Slotkin, who served three tours in Iraq alongside the US military as a CIA analyst, calls Iran's use of drones a "new era of warfare" for the United States, and urges clearer objectives from the White House. She speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Slotkin Demands Pentagon Accounting Before Backing More Funding

description: President Donald Trump says "we've got to finish the job" in Iran at Verst Logistics in Hebron, Kentucky. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says US Won't Leave Iran Early, Oil Will Come Down

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The United Nations Security Council approved a largely symbolic denunciation of Iran’s attacks on its Gulf neighbors, calling on the Islamic Republic to halt strikes that have disrupted global energy markets.
title: Top UN Body Condemns Iran Attacks Against Gulf Neighbors

author: Gonzalo Soto, Alex Vasquez
description: President Claudia Sheinbaum’s attempt to overhaul Mexico’s electoral system fell short of the needed support for approval in the lower house of Congress on Wednesday, marking the first legislative setback in her agenda of priority reforms.
title: Mexico Rejects Electoral Bill, Sheinbaum’s First Defeat in Congress

author: Joe Sobczyk
description: It’s not clear yet whether drawing down stockpiles will lower prices.
title: More Oil Coming to Ease Supply Pinch Caused by Iran War

author: Ari Natter, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump indicated he would tap the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve to help ease oil prices that have soared amid the war with Iran and threaten to further squeeze American households worried about costs of living.
title: Trump Signals US Will Tap Oil Reserve to Ease Price Shock

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union warned that its inflation rate could surpass 3% this year if the war in the Middle East causes Brent oil prices to remain around $100 per barrel and gas prices stay elevated for an extended period.
title: EU Warns Iran Conflict Could Push the Bloc’s Inflation Above 3%

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Yelena Shulyatyeva, senior US economist at The Conference Board, on the morning's tame CPI report Then,  BNY Chief Investment Officer Jason Granet discusses the broader market impact of the war with Iran and dropping oil production. Plus, Antimony CEO Gary Evans breaks down what his critical minerals company plans to do with a $27 million grant from the Department of Defense as the US government sures up its materials stockpile. Then, Bloomberg's Gerry Doyle on Iran's drone arsenal and what it means for the Pentagon's strategy as strikes continue across the Middle East. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Tame CPI Overshadowed by Oil Moves, Traders Weigh War Impact | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/11/26

author: Miguel Ambriz
description: Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal introduced legislation Wednesday targeting prediction markets, the latest effort by lawmakers to crack down on the fast-growing industry over concerns about insider trading, violent-event wagers and consumer protections.
title: Blumenthal Steps Up Lawmaker Opposition to Prediction Markets

description: President Donald Trump said he didn’t believe Iran was laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and repeated his suggestion that the war would end soon, even as the confirmation of an emergency oil release did little to calm volatile markets. Asked Wednesday whether Iran had laid mines in the strait, Trump told reporters, “We don’t think so.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Encourages Oil Companies to Use Strait of Hormuz

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, Senator Rand Paul, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Republican Congressman Patrick McHenry. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Touts Strikes on Iran | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/11/2026

author: Greg Stohr
description: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court to let his administration scrap a legal shield that protects 350,000 Haitians from deportation.
title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Open Haitians to Deportation

author: David Feliba
description: Ambitious goals from Argentina’s government to bring down country risk are at odds with reality and may have caused it to miss a window to return to debt markets, investors say.
title: Argentina Missed Early Window to Sell Bonds, Investors Say

author: Ben Bartenstein, Donato Paolo Mancini, Samy Adghirni
description: Iran has told regional intermediaries that for a ceasefire, the US must guarantee that neither it nor Israel will strike the country in the future, according to several officials familiar with the matter.
title: Iran Says Truce Depends on US, Israel Pledging Not to Strike

author: Joe Mathieu, Matt Shirley, Amanda Hayes Roark
description: Markwayne Mullin is expected to face tough public questioning next week from fellow Republican Rand Paul, whose Senate committee has tremendous influence over Mullin’s path to confirmation as President Donald Trump’s next Homeland Security secretary.
title: Rand Paul Draws Line for Mullin’s DHS Hearing: ‘This Is America’

description: The Iran War is sending a dangerous message to North Korea about nuclear weapons, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Karishma Vaswani says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kim Jong Un’s Lesson From Iran

author: Jack Wittels
description: Fuel tanks at the Port of Salalah have been struck by drones, the state-run Oman News Agency reported, citing a security source.
title: Operations Suspended at Oman Port as Drones Hit Fuel Tanks

author: Beatriz Reis
description: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro tied President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a simulated October runoff, the latest sign a series of corruption scandals are weighing on the leftist leader’s reelection bid in Brazil.
title: Bolsonaro, Lula Tie in Potential Brazil Runoff, Poll Shows

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump said the massive release of emergency oil reserves approved by the International Energy Agency would ease energy price pressures while the US seeks to “finish the job” in its campaign against Iran.
title: Trump Touts Oil Supply Moves, Vows to Finish the Job in Iran

author: Amara Omeokwe
description: The top Republican on the Senate Banking Committee said the “head prosecutor” handling the Department of Justice’s criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell had been replaced, a potentially notable shift in the highly consequential probe.
title: GOP Senator Says Prosecutor in Powell Probe Has Been Changed

author: Patricia Garip, James Attwood
description: Chile just inaugurated a right-wing president who will quickly signal his intention to bring the copper-rich country into closer alignment with the administration of US head of state Donald Trump.
title: Chile’s New President to Signal Swift Alignment With Trump

description: The IEA is considering releasing oil barrels from reserves with brent over $90, though mixed messages from US officials were met with market volatility. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: IEA Looks at Releasing Oil Reserves as Iran War Chokes Supply

author: Erin Hudson
description: A hotly contested election in Montclair, New Jersey, to increase taxes for the town’s cash-strapped public school system was too close to call as of Wednesday morning, according to county officials.
title: Montclair’s Vote to Hike Taxes for Schools Too Close to Call

author: Shruti Srivastava
description: India’s decision to ease investment rules for neighboring countries may reopen the door to Chinese capital, but strict ownership limits mean large firms such as BYD Co. and Great Wall Motor Co. will still face same screening requirements.
title: India Investment Easing Offers Limited Opening to Chinese Firms

author: Gerry Doyle, Ellen Milligan
description: Iran’s ability to make more Shahed-136 weapons, rudimentary cruise missiles it has used to attack targets around the Persian Gulf, has been reduced by US and Israeli air strikes, but stockpiles remain and making more requires no complex components.
title: Iran’s Production of Shahed Missiles Slowed Down But Not Halted

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia’s capital has been facing widespread mobile internet outages, as authorities appear to be testing further controls over the country’s web infrastructure.
title: Moscow Internet Shutdowns Test Russia’s Expanding Web Controls

author: Rene Vollgraaff
description: South Africa’s health minister suspended the head of his department and two other senior officials who were charged with fraud earlier this month.
title: South Africa Suspends Three Fraud-Accused Health Officials

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany expects to release part of its national oil reserves if a proposal by the International Energy Agency is accepted, Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said.
title: Germany Says Ready to Release Part of National Oil Reserve

author: Bilal Hussain, Tooba Khan
description: The US-Israeli attacks are shaking Islamabad’s delicate web of global alliances.
title: Iran War Has Pakistan Walking on Eggshells

description: The International Energy Agency is proposing a release of emergency oil reserves that would be the largest in its history, with a decision possible later on Wednesday, according to a person familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Anthony di Paola has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: IEA Proposes Largest Oil Stockpiles Release in Its History

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany’s economy is expected to suffer only a minor setback from the war in Iran if the conflict doesn’t escalate further, according to the German Institute for Economic Research in Berlin.
title: Germany Can Weather Iran War If It Doesn’t Last, Institute Says

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said her country will not participate in the US-Israeli attacks on Iran, and is instead seeking to help with a diplomatic resolution.
title: Italy Won’t Join US-Israeli Attacks on Iran, Meloni Says

author: Tom Redmond, Niki Koswanage
description: Malaysia’s cabinet received a report on the probe into anti-graft chief Azam Baki’s shareholdings and referred the matter to the chief secretary to the government to follow up.
title: Malaysia Taps Senior Official to Take Next Steps on Graft Chief

author: Andra Timu, Eric Martin
description: Romania is set to approve a US request to temporarily deploy fighter jets at a Black Sea airbase to help with its military operations in the Middle East, people familiar with the matter said.
title: Romania Set to Allow US to Use Black Sea Base for Iran Missions

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s party narrowed its double-digit deficit in a new poll after intensifying his campaign less than five weeks until an election, though the opposition Tisza party held a 14-point lead.
title: Hungarian Opposition Lead Narrows as Orban Intensifies Campaign

description: The US war effort against Iran is showing signs of strain as Iran's arsenal of missiles and drones has forced the US to dig deep into inventories of expensive interceptors. Tehran is still hitting valuable military installations and energy infrastructure across the Middle East daily. Bloomberg Economics Defense Lead Becca Wasser breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How Iran's Weaponry Can Put US Military Under Strain

author: Alex Morales
description: The UK government is preparing to publish a first set of documents relating to the controversial appointment of Peter Mandelson as US ambassador in a move that threatens to redouble pressure on Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
title: UK to Release Trove of Mandelson Papers as Starmer Faces Heat

author: Rene Vollgraaff
description: The new US ambassador to South Africa said President Donald Trump is running out of patience with Pretoria over its failure to address Washington’s demands for policy changes, Netwerk24 reported.
title: Envoy Warns US Patience With South Africa Is Waning, N24 Says

author: Katarina Hoije, Momar Niang
description: To read this article in English, click here.
title: La Fracture Faye-Sonko Tombe Mal Pour la Dette du Sénégal

author: Arsalan Shahla, Galit Altstein
description: World governments stepped up efforts to calm energy markets as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a pivotal supply route, showed no sign of ending and Iran continued attacks across the region.
title: World Races to Shield Oil Flows After Iran War Hits Supplies

description:
On today's show, Bloomberg looks at the Middle East conflict and how the US war effort is showing unexpected signs of strain against an adversary whose military budget is smaller than the GDP of Vermont - but which has an arsenal of missiles and drones unlike anything the US has ever faced.

Oil prices held below $90 a barrel despite a Wall Street Journal report that the IEA proposed the largest crude reserve release in its history. It rebounded from lows after the White House acknowledged that a post from Energy Secretary Chris Wright was wrong in claiming an oil tanker had been escorted by the US Navy through the Strait of Hormuz.

And Oracle shares rallied in extended trading after the company posted strong results and gave an outlook that suggested there is little letup in demand for AI computing. 

Today's guest: Michelle Wiese Bockmann, Windward, Senior Maritime Intelligence Analyst. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Military Under Strain From Iran War; China Moves to Limit OpenClaw AI | Daybreak Europe 3/11/2026

author: Rodrigo Orihuela
description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez dismissed concerns over US President Donald Trump’s threats to cut trade off trade ties with Spain.
title: Sánchez Rejects Trump’s Threat to Cut Off US Trade With Spain

author: Lars Paulsson, Charlie Duxbury
description: Sweden is unlikely to offer financial support for Stegra AB even as the startup races to secure funding for its first factory by the end of this month, according to a senior lawmaker whose party underpins the ruling coalition.
title: Swedish Lawmaker Downplays Stegra Aid as Funding Needs Jump

description: President Donald Trump warned Iran against laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz. He said the US would use the same capabilities it deployed against alleged drug-running boats in the Caribbean Sea “to permanently eliminate any boat or ship attempting to mine the Hormuz Strait.” Trump also said the US had destroyed 10 “inactive mine laying boats and/or ships” in the last few hours. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.
title: US Warns Iran Against Laying Mines in Strait of Hormuz

description:
Mosharraf Zaidi, the Pakistani Prime Minister's Spokesperson for Foreign Media, says Islamabad will come to Riyadh's aid whenever needed. His comments come as Iran retaliates against US-Israeli strikes by targeting Gulf nations. Zaidi appeared on Bloomberg’s Insight with Haslinda Amin.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pakistan Ready to Support Saudi After Iran Attacks, Says PM's Spokesman

author: Gerry Doyle, Peter Martin
description: From drone barrages to strikes on missile launchers, the strategies shaping the conflict reflect experience gained by the US, Israel and Iran in 2025.
title: Iran War Tactics Evolve From Past Conflict’s Lessons

author: Katarina Hoije, Momar Niang
description: A widening rift between Senegal’s top leaders risks splitting the ruling party and stoking renewed uncertainty as the nation contends with ballooning debt and negotiates a new International Monetary Fund program.
title: Senegal’s Widening Ruling Party Rift Risks Clouding Debt Outlook

description: Chinese officials are frustrated by what they see as insufficient US preparation for Donald Trump's upcoming meeting with Xi Jinping, according to a person familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: China Said to Be Irked by Xi-Trump Summit Planning

author: Haslinda Amin, Tooba Khan
description: Pakistan will come to the “aid” of Saudi Arabia whenever needed, while the South Asian country makes efforts to ensure stability in the Middle East, Prime Minister’s spokesperson said.
title: Pakistan Says Will Be There Before It Is Needed for Saudi Arabia

author: Thomas Seal
description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is closing in on a majority in Parliament after a fourth lawmaker defected to his ruling Liberal Party.
title: Canada PM Carney Approaches Majority With Fourth Defecting Rival

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: North Korea test-fired cruise missiles from its latest warship, the second time in a week it has launched its new sea-to-surface weapons system as reports grow that the US is shifting air defense assets out of South Korea to help it fight Iran.
title: N. Korea Tests Missiles as US Reportedly Moves Arms to Mideast
Oil Fluctuates After Report of IEA Reserve Release

author: Lauren Dezenski
description: Incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, is projected to win the Republican Senate primary in Mississippi, according to AP.
title: Hyde-Smith Wins Mississippi GOP Senate Primary, AP Projects

author: Brett Pulley, Bill Allison
description: In one of the most conservative congressional districts in the US, a special election to replace former Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene has produced an unusual runoff: a Democrat facing a Republican endorsed by President Donald Trump.
title: Georgia Democrat Leads Vote in Marjorie Taylor Greene’s District

author: Eamon Farhat
description: The cost of meeting net zero is less than a single fossil fuel price shock, the UK’s official climate adviser said.
title: Net Zero Costs Less Than One Fossil Fuel Shock, UK’s CCC Says
